meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen saw a zero on his phone, in class, before anyone called me. Explain that.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
He wrote it over the weekend somewhere else and pasted it in. I'm writing those times down.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Is that the only document, or is there more?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote from memory, or from a different edition. Is that what you're calling proof?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. Isn't that what revising is?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. I'll agree to the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. Put the time in the email tonight and I'll confirm it with Owen.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that agreement in writing, with the time, and I will confirm it with Owen. I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight with the time. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You put the quote from the essay beside the play and told her to search the scene herself, which gave her something she could check, and you answered her misquote defence on the spot.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the zero first and showed documents instead of a score.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its 11:31 PM, 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM entries the night before the essay was due, landed very close to that night, though it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students change their argument between an outline and an essay, answer that point before offering the rewrite, for example by saying the essay never mentions cowardice and you have no draft showing the change.
